data.name: Help_Approve
data.value:
Usage: {0} approve --plant <folder> --machine <host>… [--run <id>] --role "<role>" --record "<reference>" [--name "<name>"] [--date <yyyy-MM-dd>]
Records a run (default: the newest) as the approved state of each machine, for example after commissioning, a site acceptance test or a vendor visit. --record is your change, QMS or approval reference.
Exit codes: 0 success, 3 error.

data.name: Help_Baseline
data.value:
Usage: {0} baseline <subcommand> --plant <folder> …
import <path> --name <name> import a customer baseline (GPO backup folder, riegel.baseline/1 JSON or CSV) list [--format text|json] imported baselines remove <id> remove an imported baseline
Exit codes: 0 success, 3 error.

data.name: Help_Check
data.value:
Usage: {0} check [--plant <folder>] [--snapshot <file>…|--this-pc] [options]
Evaluates snapshots (or this PC) against the catalogue. Without --plant it only evaluates and prints. With --plant it applies the plant's registers, stores the run, and compares it with the previous run and the approved state.
--plant <folder> plant folder; created if missing --snapshot <file>… exports (.snapshot.json, .json.gz) or builtin bundle folders; several allowed --this-pc collect this PC first (Windows; the default there without --snapshot) --no-store with --plant: evaluate and compare, but write nothing --brief one line per machine for Icinga/Nagios, with performance data --format text|json output format (default: text) --alert change|state change (default with --plant) or state (default without) --critical <list> tokens for exit code 2, comma-separated; replaces the list; none = no token --warning <list> tokens for exit code 1; replaces the list
Tokens: regression, newhigh, high, medium, low, expired, expiring, pending, overdue, incomplete, stale, clock change: critical regression,newhigh · warning expired,expiring,pending,overdue,incomplete,stale,clock state: critical regression,high · warning medium,low,expired,expiring,pending,overdue,incomplete,stale,clock Exit codes: 0 OK, 1 WARNING, 2 CRITICAL, 3 UNKNOWN.

data.name: Help_Collect
data.value:
Usage: {0} collect [--out <folder>] [--gzip] [--minimal] [--deep] [--pseudonymize]
Windows only. Writes a snapshot of this PC (<HOST>_<time>.snapshot.json and .sha256). Reads only and changes no configuration; run it in an elevated console for a complete snapshot.
--out <folder> target folder (default: current folder) --gzip write .snapshot.json.gz --minimal no child processes (no secedit, no gpresult), no Windows Update query, firewall profiles only --deep also query the LSASS process protection --pseudonymize replace host, account and path names
Exit codes: 0 complete, 1 written but incomplete (not elevated or items denied), 3 nothing written.

data.name: Help_CollectionRecord
data.value:
Usage: {0} collection-record --plant <folder> [--import <id>|--latest] [--out <folder>] [--language <code>]
Writes the collection record of an import (default: the latest) for sign-off: exports with hashes, collector, options, the collecting and witness roles and signature lines.
Exit codes: 0 success, 3 error.

data.name: Help_Collector
data.value:
Usage: {0} collector export <folder>
Windows only. Copies the portable collector bundle with a hand-over note (UEBERGABE.txt: hashes, version, date, how to run it, what it leaves behind) to a USB stick or a share.
Exit codes: 0 success, 3 error.

data.name: Help_Compare
data.value:
Usage: {0} compare --plant <folder> --machine <host> [--against previous|approved] [--format text|json]
Shows the status changes and raw-value drift between the newest run of a machine and its previous run (default) or its approved state.
Exit codes: 0 success, 3 error (for example, no approved state).

data.name: Help_CompareSnapshot
data.value:
Usage: {0} compare-snapshot <fresh-snapshot> --evidence <zip> [--host <host>] [--format text|json]
Auditor sampling: compares a freshly collected snapshot with the packed snapshot of the same machine in an evidence pack, leaving out volatile values.
Exit codes: 0 consistent, 1 differs, 3 error.

data.name: Help_Exceptions
data.value:
Usage: {0} exceptions <subcommand> --plant <folder> …
validate [--format text|json] check the register; exit 0 valid, 1 warnings, 2 invalid list [--format text|json] all exceptions with their state expiring [--days <n>] [--format text|json] expiring and expired exceptions (default: the plant's warnDays) approval-sheet [--ids <id>…|--pending] [--out <folder>] [--language <code>] approval sheet (PDF); default: all pending entries approve --ids <id>… --role "<role>" --record "<reference>" [--review-by <yyyy-MM-dd>] [--date <yyyy-MM-dd>] [--name "<name>"] enter a signed approval; a review date is required import-template <template.json|name> add a template's entries as pending exceptions built-in: beispiel-anlagenbau
Exit codes: 0 success, 3 error; validate as above.

data.name: Help_ExitCodes
data.value: Exit codes: 0 OK, 1 WARNING, 2 CRITICAL, 3 UNKNOWN (usage error, unreadable or corrupt snapshot, checksum mismatch, I/O error). check and import alert on change with --plant (critical: regression,newhigh) and on state without (critical: regression,high). verify: 0 reproduced, 2 mismatch · compare-snapshot: 0 consistent, 1 differs · validate: 0 valid, 1 warnings, 2 invalid.

data.name: Help_Import
data.value:
Usage: {0} import <file|folder>… --plant <folder> [--collected-by-role <role>] [--witness-role <role>] [--record]
Adds exports or builtin bundles to the plant folder: checks the .sha256 files, writes the import record, evaluates and stores the runs. A checksum mismatch stops the whole import before anything is written. A folder that is not a builtin bundle (named *.riegel-builtin or holding hostname.txt or secedit.inf) stands for the exports in it (*.snapshot.json, *.snapshot.json.gz).
--plant <folder> plant folder --collected-by-role <role> role of the person who collected (import record) --witness-role <role> role of the operator's witness (import record) --record also write the collection record (PDF) --brief, --format, --alert, --critical, --warning as for check (default alert mode: change)
Exit codes as for check.

data.name: Help_Measures
data.value:
Usage: {0} measures <subcommand> --plant <folder> …
list [--format text|json] the remediation plan overdue [--format text|json] planned measures past their due date add --rule <id> --action "<text>" --owner-role "<role>" --due <yyyy-MM-dd> [--machine <host>…|--group <id>…|--all-machines] [--ticket <ref>] [--comment "<text>"] [--created-by-role "<role>"] plan a measure (default scope: all machines) close <id> [--state done|dropped] [--comment "<text>"] close a measure (default: done)
Exit codes: 0 success, 3 error.

data.name: Help_Overview
data.value:
Usage: {0} <command> [options] {0} <command> --help shows the options of a command
Check and monitor: check evaluate this PC or snapshots; with --plant: store, compare, alert on change collect Windows: write a snapshot of this PC import add exports or builtin bundles to a plant folder compare status changes and drift of one machine approve record a run as the approved state
Documents: report plant report (PDF, Excel, CSV, JSON) and evidence pack summary one-page summary across plants target-config target configuration for sign-off (PDF, Excel) collection-record collection record of an import for sign-off remediate remediation proposal as files – never applied
Registers and catalogue: exceptions validate | list | expiring | approval-sheet | approve | import-template tailoring list | validate | approve | import-template measures list | overdue | add | close baseline import | list | remove rules the rule catalogue
Auditors: verify check the hashes of an evidence pack and re-evaluate it compare-snapshot compare a fresh snapshot with the packed one
Plant folder and collector: plant init create a plant folder collector export Windows: copy the portable collector with a hand-over note
Global options: --help, --hilfe this help --version version of Riegel, collector and catalogue --info product, licence, links and data folder --licenses, --lizenzen licence texts --nur-lesen, --read-only write nothing into the plant folder (documents only to --out)

data.name: Help_Plant
data.value:
Usage: {0} plant init <folder> --name <name>
Creates a plant folder (riegel-plant.json). check --plant also creates one when the folder is missing.
Exit codes: 0 success, 3 error.

data.name: Help_Remediate
data.value:
Usage: {0} remediate --plant <folder> --machine <host> [--run <id>] [--out <folder>] [--language <code>]
Writes a remediation proposal as files only (.reg with rollback .reg, GptTmpl.inf, audit.csv, README.txt) under remediation/<host>/<run>/ in --out or in the plant folder. Riegel never applies them; agree every change with the machine vendor first.
Exit codes: 0 success, 3 error.

data.name: Help_Report
data.value:
Usage: {0} report --plant <folder> [options]
Writes the plant report and the other outputs from the newest run of each machine.
--machine <host>… only these machines --format pdf,xlsx,csv,json formats (default: pdf,xlsx); json writes the runs (results.json) --per-machine also one PDF per machine --no-appendix without the per-machine appendix --preset audit|as-delivered report preset (default: from the plant) --evidence also the evidence pack (ZIP) --include-baseline-content with --evidence: pack the content of imported baselines (check their licence) --pdfa PDF/A, if this build supports it --language <code> en, de, es, fr, zh-Hans (default: plant, then user interface) --out <folder> target folder (default: reports/<time>/ in the plant folder)
Exit codes: 0 success, 3 error.

data.name: Help_Rules
data.value:
Usage: {0} rules [--id <ID>] [--format text|json|md]
Lists the rule catalogue, or one rule with rationale, OT note, remedy and references.
Exit codes: 0 success, 3 error.

data.name: Help_ScriptsNote
data.value: In scripts and scheduled tasks use Riegel.Cli.exe: cmd and PowerShell do not wait for Riegel.exe (otherwise start /wait Riegel.exe … or Riegel.exe … | Out-Default).

data.name: Help_Summary
data.value:
Usage: {0} summary --plant <folder> [--plant <folder>…] [--out <folder>] [--language <code>]
One A4 page across plants for management: machines, supported operating systems, open high findings with trend, regressions, expiring exceptions and overdue measures. Written to --out or to the current folder.
Exit codes: 0 success, 3 error.

data.name: Help_TargetConfig
data.value:
Usage: {0} target-config --plant <folder> [--group <id>] [--out <folder>] [--language <code>]
Writes the target configuration for sign-off as PDF and Excel: per group and role the rules in scope with their expected values, the tailoring decisions, imported baselines and where the expected values come from.

Checks every hash in an evidence pack, re-evaluates the packed snapshots with the packed catalogue and registers and compares the results with the packed ones.
